newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 31.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* Shares seen slightly down after four-day Easter holiday as no positive news is expected to counter the sharp drop of the Dow Jones, says Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn.

* BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap says correction may be seen in issues which posted gains before the Easter holidays but it would be temporary as buyers are likely to step in again once desired valuations are reached.
* Market may still be weak with additional liquidity seen with the listing of Equitable Bank on April 3, said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.

* The Dow closed 140 points down to 6,740.59 points on Thursday. Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co's American Depositary Receipt settled at $59 7/8. The U.S. stock market was closed on Good Friday.
* All Asia's Alvarez adds that support for the market is seen at 3,200. BPI's Yap said that funds freed with the listing of Equitable Bank will likely be injected into thirdliner issues.

* The Philippine Central Bank has approved the applications of holding concern A. Soriano Corp (Anscor) and the Phinma Group to raise their stakes in AsianBank to a maximum of 60 percent. Anscor and Phinma have a 39.13 stake each in the bank.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer, quoting sources, says partnership of Ayala Corp and Singapore Telecommunications in Globe Telecom GMCR Inc is being threatened by managerial differences over critical issues of rollout and profitability.
* Manila Times says Singapore Telecom is raising serious questions over the direction and management of Globe Telecom.
* Fortune Cement Corp has increased its annual clinker production by about 50 percent to 750,000 tonnes as part of the second phase of its expansion programme, Manila Bulletin says.
* Engineering Equipment Inc is raising its capital to two billion pesos from 875 million pesos to fund its construction projects, reports Manila Bulletin.

* Smart Communications Co Inc expects to generate as much as nine billion pesos from its initial public offering scheduled middle of 1997. The cellular phone company said it is offering 450 million of its common shares at a price ranging from 12 pesos to 20 pesos.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index rose 19.02 points to 3,223.14. The Philippine stock and financial markets were closed on Maundy Thursday and Good Friday.
* The peso closed lower at 26.367 to the dollar vs 26.355
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was lower at 9.9375 percent from 10.03125 percent.
